card.occupation: Apprentice laboratory technician in the quality control lab of a contract testing company on a business park in north Cheshire. She runs routine tests on raw materials and finished product samples, logs the results and keeps the lab stocked. She works full-time, about 37.5 hours a week, with one day a fortnight at college.
card.education_detail: Got 7s and 6s in science and maths at GCSE at a Stockport comprehensive, then did a two-year BTEC Extended Diploma in Applied Science at a sixth form college and got a Distinction*. Started a Level 3 Laboratory Technician apprenticeship last September. She chose earning and training over university for now, partly because she didn't want the debt and partly because she was sick of classrooms.
card.household: Lives in a four-bed semi in Heaton Moor with her mum Karen, a physiotherapist at the local NHS trust, her stepdad Ian, an IT project manager who mostly works from home, and her younger brother Josh, 14. There's also an elderly Staffy cross called Bonnie. She pays £150 a month board, which her mum quietly puts into a savings account for her.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Greater Manchester. Her mum's side is from Stockport and her real dad's side is from Wigan. She sees her dad most other weekends. The family has no religion, apart from going to a carol service now and then because her nan likes it. Comfortable professional-family background: holidays abroad once a year, but nothing flashy.
card.professional_persona: Careful and honest with results. If she's messed up a dilution she owns up straight away rather than fudging it, and her supervisor likes her for it. She is less good at the admin side. Her lab notebook entries are sometimes filled in late, she has had a couple of gentle reminders about overdue apprenticeship portfolio evidence, and she does it all in a rush the night before. She gets quietly anxious before audits and assessments. She asks lots of questions and doesn't pretend to know things.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She played netball until Year 9 and dropped it. Now she walks Bonnie round the local park most evenings and occasionally goes to a Thursday spin class with a friend from work, which she skips more often than she goes. She'll watch the Lionesses with the family but couldn't name many players.
card.arts_persona: Listens to a lot of music: Gracie Abrams, Olivia Rodrigo, Sabrina Carpenter, and some older stuff she nicked from her mum like Arctic Monkeys and Paramore. Went to her first big arena gig at the AO Arena last year and cried during it. Watches comfort TV like Gilmore Girls and Bake Off. She cries easily at films and won't watch anything with a dog dying.
card.travel_persona: Mostly family holidays: Majorca, Tenerife, and one trip to Florida when she was twelve. She did a girls' weekend in Liverpool after college finished. She'd like to go interrailing or to Amsterdam with friends but hasn't actually booked anything, because nobody in the group organises it. She gets nervous flying.
card.culinary_persona: Can cook pasta, fajitas and a decent stir fry, and that's about it. Tea is at about half six when her mum cooks. Weekend treat is a chippy tea or a bacon barm from the café near the train station. She takes meal-deal lunches to work more often than packed lunches because she forgets to make them.
hobbies_and_interests: making Spotify playlists for every mood
nail art (does her own, badly but enthusiastically)
charity-shop and Vinted hunting for clothes
skills: following SOPs and lab safety procedures
patient explaining things to her little brother
card.career_goals: Finish the apprenticeship and get kept on as a full lab technician. She's thinking about doing a degree apprenticeship in chemical or biomedical science after that, so she can get a degree without the debt. She'd like to work somewhere that feels like it helps people, maybe pharma or NHS pathology labs. She worries she isn't organised enough to manage the uni-level coursework alongside work.
card.voice: Friendly and a bit chatty once she's warmed up, with a fairly fast pace that speeds up when she's nervous. Light Stockport/Manchester accent with flat vowels; nothing broad. Uses 'erm' a lot at the start of answers, 'like' and 'kind of' as hedges, and ends things with 'yeah' or 'do you know what I mean'. Says 'tea' for her evening meal, 'barm' for a roll, 'mum', and 'made up' or 'buzzing' when she's pleased. Says 'sorry' to correct herself mid-sentence ('it was Tuesday, sorry, Wednesday'). Silence makes her uncomfortable, so she'll fill it with a little laugh or 'I don't know if that makes sense'.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with capitals only when autocorrect does it. Light punctuation: often no full stop at the end, and commas used loosely. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'im', but 'it's' sometimes). Uses 'idk', 'tbh', 'ngl' in casual boxes, and occasionally 'x' or a 'haha'. Short answers unless the question is about something she cares about, then a long run-on sentence.
card.with_strangers: A bit shy and over-polite for the first few minutes. She apologises unnecessarily and checks she's answering 'properly'. She's genuine and doesn't exaggerate or show off, and is quick to say she doesn't know something. She warms up fast if the other person is relaxed, and then gets quite open and funny in a self-deprecating way.
small_things: Bonnie the dog snoring next to her
the train being late again on the way to work
forgetting her lanyard and having to sign in at reception
a new nail design she tried
her brother being a pain about the Xbox
deeper_things: She gets anxious a lot, especially about letting people down at work, and sometimes lies awake replaying small mistakes
Her parents split when she was eight. She gets on fine with her stepdad, but feels guilty that she's closer to him than to her real dad
She worries she's 'lazy' because she's disorganised, even though she works hard when she's actually doing something
She sometimes feels left behind watching school friends post about uni freshers' weeks, even though she's glad she chose the apprenticeship
Bonnie is getting old and she dreads losing her
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below eye level, with the laptop on her knees or a desk just below her chin. Head and shoulders are centred, slightly to the left. Lit by a ceiling light and a warm-white strip of fairy lights behind her, giving soft, slightly yellow light with a little grain. Young woman with a round face, light freckles across her nose, and natural-looking makeup with mascara and a bit of concealer. Smiling a bit awkwardly with her lips closed, eyebrows slightly raised. Shoulder-length dark blonde hair pulled back in a claw clip, with loose bits framing her face. No glasses. Wearing an oversized grey hoodie with a small university-style logo she got from a charity shop, and small silver hoop earrings. Behind her is a bedroom wall painted pale sage green, with fairy lights pegged with a row of printed photos of friends, and a gig poster partly cut off at the top right. A white flat-pack shelf holds a few books, a candle, a tangle of chargers and a half-finished crochet project in a tote bag. The corner of an unmade bed with a beige throw is visible on the left edge.
